label: PF Backlog 436
title: B6: WASM plugins

analysis.implementation_strategy: Extend the existing plugin infrastructure (`core/plugins.py`, `core/execution_contract.py`, `core/skill_contracts.py`, `core/task_contract.py`, `config/plugins-registry.json`) with a WASM plugin runtime. The existing Python-based plugin contract defines the interfaces; the WASM runtime adds an alternative execution backend that loads `.wasm` modules and maps the existing contracts (execution, skill, task) onto WASM guest exports. Reuse the plugin registry JSON as the declaration format — add a `runtime: wasm` field. The Rust toolchain (shared with BI-PF-0404) compiles guest modules; the host side uses a WASI-compatible runtime (e.g. wasmtime via Python binding or sidecar). The WASM plugin contract must be a strict subset or superset of the current Python plugin contract to maintain compatibility.
dependency_findings: REQUIRES BI-PF-0391 (Epic B) architecture decisions on plugin decomposition.
RELATED BI-PF-0404 (Rust components) — shared Rust/WASM toolchain.
RELATED BI-PF-0406 (service decomposition) — WASM plugins may later run in isolated services; contract should be service-ready.
RELATED BI-PF-0402 (persistence adapters) — if WASM plugins need persistence access, they should go through the adapter contract.
conflict_findings: Build-system conflict with BI-PF-0404: both introduce Rust toolchain. Coordinate toolchain version and CI jobs.
core/plugins.py is touched by this item; no other item in this batch modifies it.
config/plugins-registry.json schema extension may conflict if other items add registry fields; coordinate schema evolution.
duplication_findings: No existing WASM runtime in the codebase — no duplication.
core/plugins.py already implements a plugin loader; WASM support should be an additional backend, not a replacement — avoid duplicating registry/loading logic.
BI-PF-0404 (Rust components) introduces Rust toolchain; WASM guest modules also need Rust (or another WASM-targeting language) toolchain — share build infra, don't duplicate.
core/execution_contract.py, core/skill_contracts.py, core/task_contract.py define the plugin interfaces — WASM plugins must conform to these, not create parallel contracts.
analysis.rationale: Existing plugin contract and registry provide clear extension points. The item adds an alternative execution backend rather than rewriting the plugin system. Key decisions are the WASM host runtime and the host-function import surface, which a human must approve.
assumptions: Existing Python plugins continue to work unchanged; WASM is an additive runtime, not a replacement.
Plugin registry JSON schema is extensible without breaking current entries.
The WASM guest model uses WASI (or a subset) for I/O and host-function imports for PF-specific capabilities (execution, skill, task).
Rust is the primary guest language, but the design should not preclude other languages targeting WASM.
risks: WASM host runtime choice (wasmtime, wasmer, WAMR) is a significant architectural decision with performance and compatibility trade-offs.
Existing Python plugin contract may not map cleanly to WASM guest model (memory isolation, host function imports).
Performance overhead of WASM host invocation vs direct Python plugin calls may be non-trivial for small plugins.
Guest plugin toolchain (Rust→WASM) raises the bar for plugin authors.
Security: WASM sandboxing is a benefit but host-function import surface must be carefully curated.
evidence: Candidate code lists 4 existing contract modules and the plugin registry — clear extension points.
Item body trigger: 'plugin contract + need' — a concrete demand exists.
BI-PF-0388 ADR confirms compiled-editions approach compatible with WASM runtime inclusion.
